statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, which the prior hour declared as its narrow danger window, resolved benignly: NQ is at 29,280.00, +0.08%, inside a 40.75-point range of 29,247.75-29,288.50 as of 22:16 UTC, so the first post-FOMC price discovery after the CME maintenance halt is two-sided rather than one-way. Tail eases to 16 on that observed path. Stress stays in the high band at 73 because the 10-year settled at 5.021%, its highest since 2007, the 2-year sits at 4.736% against a 4.742% 52-week high, and the Fed's projections point to at least one further hike this year.
recommendation: Tail falls to the low band on observed evidence rather than assumption. The reopen after the CME maintenance halt produced a 40.75-point two-sided band, which is the specific structure the prior hour identified as the test of whether post-FOMC repricing was unfinished. Implied volatility decayed from an 18.94 session high to a 17.71 close, and crude fell about 3.2% to settle near $102 on reported progress toward restarting the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline. Three amplifiers remain unresolved and are the reason Stress stays high while Tail eases: a 10-year above 5% for the first time since 2007, a 2-year pinned within a basis point of its 52-week high, and a narrow leadership profile in which the Dow fell 1.21% and the S&P 500 0.45% while the Nasdaq-100 closed 0.02% higher. The declared danger window is the 13:30-14:30 UTC cash open on September 17, the first full regular session after the policy shift, where one-way structure would establish if it is going to. No high-impact U.S. release falls in the next seven days now that the FOMC has passed; the nearest cluster is four medium-impact prints at 12:30 UTC on September 17.
headline: Post-FOMC Globex reopen is two-sided at 29,280.00 inside a 40-point band, returning Tail to the low band while a 5.021% 10-year keeps Stress high
body: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% at 18:00 UTC in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase in three years, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the 2 percent goal. Chair Warsh reinforced the hawkish framing at his press conference, saying inflation is too high and has been for too long, and the Summary of Economic Projections showed most participants expecting at least one further 25 basis point hike before year-end. The decisive evidence for this hour arrived after the prior assessment. CME's maintenance halt ended at 22:00 UTC and the reference contract reopened: NQ is at 29,280.00, up 23.25 points or 0.08%, inside a 40.75-point range of 29,247.75-29,288.50 as of 22:16 UTC. That is an orderly, balanced auction rather than a continuation of the post-press-conference leg that carried the index from 29,235.89 to a 28,753.29 low, and it is the direct resolution of the danger window the prior hour declared. Combined with the 192-point recovery into the 28,945.06 cash close, the pathological no-retracement path scored at 19:00 UTC has now been invalidated twice. What has not resolved is the rates channel, and it has in fact worsened relative to the prior assessment. The 10-year settled at 5.021%, above 5% for the first time since 2007, having traded 4.937-5.029 against a 5.041 52-week high. The 2-year finished at 4.736% after a 4.602-4.742 range, leaving it within a basis point of its 52-week high with 14 basis points of intraday front-end repricing unretraced. A second unresolved amplifier is breadth: the Dow fell 631.21 points or 1.21% to 51,461.90 and the S&P 500 lost 0.45% to 7,551.81 while the Nasdaq-100 closed 0.02% higher, so the index is being held up by a narrow megacap cohort rather than a broad tape. Semiconductors were the visible source of that support, rallying on a Reuters-sourced report that SK Hynix is in exploratory talks with Intel about manufacturing memory chips in the United States. The third channel is energy. WTI settled near $102 and Brent near $105, down about 3.2% and 2.7%, after U.S. officials said the Saudi East-West pipeline damaged in a September 11 drone attack would restart within days; independent analysts reading satellite imagery of the damaged pumping station argue the outage could last weeks. With four million barrels per day of capacity at stake, that disagreement is an open overnight headline channel and is the reason the modelled overnight floor sits slightly above a typical quiet night. Taken together, the observed price path supports the low band while three unresolved cross-asset channels keep Stress high, which is why this assessment separates a low Tail from a high Stress rather than easing both. The shared Finviz context file was not usable this hour: it reported collectionStatus partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, and at 118 minutes old it fell outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours the Claude state opened at 15 at Tuesday's 22:00 UTC hour, eased through the low band overnight and bottomed at 13 at 01:00 UTC while the Asian and European sessions held a contained normal range, running 14-16 through the European morning. It returned to the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the U.S. pre-market, held 20-22 through the afternoon and rose to 24 at 18:00 UTC as the FOMC statement landed. The highest reading of the window was 31 at 19:00 UTC, published while the index sat at its session low during the Warsh press conference with no retracement yet formed. That reading captured the structure observed at the time; the 192-point recovery into the 28,945.06 cash close then invalidated its continuation premise and the 20:00 UTC reading fell back to 20. The 21:00 UTC hour published 18 during the CME maintenance halt, and the current hour steps down again to 16 now that the reopen has been observed.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 16 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed reopen structure, and holds 16-17 across the Asian session. That overnight floor sits slightly above a typical quiet night because the disputed Saudi pipeline repair timeline remains an open headline channel, not because of any observed index structure. The path drifts to 17-19 through the European pre-open and morning as liquidity returns and European rates desks price the Fed's projected additional hike, then rises to 22 for the 12:00 UTC hour containing jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed index, housing starts and building permits. It peaks at 24 for the 13:00 UTC hour holding the 13:30 UTC cash open, the highest modelled value in the window and the declared danger window, because a post-policy-shift opening auction is where persistent one-way structure would establish if it is going to. That peak is explicitly conditional and rests on no observed structure. The path then decays through 23, 21 and 20 across the U.S. morning, returns to the low band at 19 through the early afternoon, ticks to 20 for the power hour on end-of-day rebalancing risk, and falls to 16 for the 21:00 UTC CME maintenance halt, where the absence of price discovery is structural rather than directional.
